    What is Robert Mueller doing now?

    AI Overview
    Robert Mueller, 81, is retired from the practice of law and is battling Parkinson’s disease, diagnosed in the summer of 2021
    . He stepped down from his role at the law firm WilmerHale and concluded his teaching career at the end of 2022, according to his family. He is no longer involved in public investigations. 
    Key Details on Current Status: 
    • Health and Retirement: Mueller, the former FBI Director and Special Counsel, retired from legal practice at the end of 2021.
    • Diagnosis: His family disclosed in September 2025 that he has been battling Parkinson’s disease since 2021.
    • Recent Activity:
      Following the special counsel investigation, he returned to WilmerHale briefly in 2019 and taught at his law school alma mater during the falls of 2021 and 2022 before retiring completely.
    • Congressional Subpoena: A House Oversight committee subpoena for his testimony regarding the Epstein case was withdrawn due to his health issues.

      Illness and death

      Robert Trump died at New York–Presbyterian Hospital in Manhattan the next day, August 15, at age 71. The New York Times quoted a family friend as saying that Trump had recently started experiencing intracerebral hemorrhaging after a fall.
